summary.en: Maduro faces a revived U.S. torture case as prosecutors invoke a rarely used law and indict him for ordering torture of rivals, while the United States has lifted sanctions on the National Assembly leader and deployed Space Force electromagnetic and electronic warfare systems against Venezuela. The Trump administration is planning changes to Delcy Rodríguez's government and the oil sector, and a Dutch security report warns that Venezuela's instability could threaten Curaçao and the wider Caribbean Kingdom. Opposition groups are mobilising nationwide protests demanding elections and the return of Machado, while workers press the government for real wage recovery. 2 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2007, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Maduro står overfor en gjenopplivet amerikansk tortur-sak etter at påtalemyndighetene har brukt en sjelden lov og tiltalt ham for å ha beordret tortur av rivaler, mens USA har opphevet sanksjoner mot lederen for nasjonalforsamlingen og satt i drift elektromagnetiske og elektroniske krigssystemer fra Space Force mot Venezuela. Trump-administrasjonen planlegger endringer i Delcy Rodríguez’ regjering og i oljesektoren, og en nederlandsk sikkerhetsrapport advarer om at Venezuelas ustabilitet kan true Curaçao og det bredere Karibiske kongeriket. Opposisjonsgrupper mobiliserer landsomfattende protester som krever valg og tilbakekalling av Machado, mens arbeidere presser regjeringen for reell lønnsgjenoppretting. To dødsfall knyttet til kamp ble registrert i 2007, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Crisis in Venezuela
background.extract: An ongoing socioeconomic and political crisis began in Venezuela during the presidencies of Hugo Chávez, Nicolás Maduro and Delcy Rodríguez. It has been marked by hyperinflation, starvation, disease, crime, and mortality rates, resulting in massive emigration. Food shortages and hyperinflation have ended, but inflation remains high. It is the worst economic crisis in Venezuela's history and considered by some sources as more severe than the Great Depression in the United States, the 1985–1994 Brazilian economic crisis, or the 2008–2009 hyperinflation in Zimbabwe. In 2019, the Institute of International Finance called it the single largest economic collapse outside of war in 45 years. Writers have compared aspects, such as unemployment and GDP contraction, to Bosnia and Herzegovina after the 1992–95 Bosnian War, and those in Russia, Cuba and Albania following the Revolutions of 1989.
